Hero.panelTitle: Taking the technology off people's hands so they can just work.
Hero.panelText: Good support is not measured by how many tickets are open, but by whether someone can get back to work in five minutes. That takes two things: actually finding the cause instead of clicking the symptom away — and then writing it down so nobody has to ask again.

About.title: About me
About.eyebrow: From building an office from scratch to daily technical practice
About.lead: My strength is not a single product but dealing with technology that is currently broken: isolate it, find the cause, fix it and write it down so it goes faster next time.
paragraphs: My first technical role was as a system administrator's assistant at “UkrZoloto” in Kyiv. We brought a new office online completely — workstations, servers, switches, network cabling, UPS units and printers. I installed and configured Windows on every machine and handed the finished workplaces over to colleagues. That is where I learned how much technology you can take off someone's hands so they can simply get on with their work.

Then came a degree in economic cybernetics (recognised by ZAB as equivalent to a German bachelor's) and 1st place among roughly 6,000 participants in the JS/FE Pre-School course by RS School and EPAM — the one externally verifiable measure of how fast I pick up new things. For about three years I have been building and operating my own technical projects daily; analysing failures and restoring service is routine.

Honest about my limits: I have not worked much with Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft 365 at administration level, and I have not used a ticketing system professionally. I am closing both gaps deliberately — MS-900 is my next certification target. What I do bring reliably: I learn fast, I do not give up before the cause is found, and I can explain technology without jargon.
